rules.title: Noindexed pages listed in the sitemap
rules.description: Pages carrying noindex (meta robots or X-Robots-Tag) are listed in the sitemap. Sitemaps should contain canonical URLs you want indexed.
rules.fix: Remove noindex pages from the sitemap, or remove noindex if they should be indexed.
rules.verify: Re-crawl; no sitemap URL should carry noindex.

rules.title: Pages excluded with noindex
rules.description: These pages carry noindex and will be dropped from search results once recrawled. Listed for review; often intentional.
rules.fix: Confirm each noindex is intentional. Remove it from pages that should rank.

rules.title: noindex on a page that robots.txt blocks
rules.description: A page intended to be noindexed is blocked by robots.txt, so crawlers never see the noindex; the URL can still be indexed from links.
rules.fix: Allow crawling of the URL so the noindex can be read, or remove the URL from the index via other means.
rules.verify: Test the URL against robots.txt and fetch it to confirm noindex is visible.

rules.title: Sitemap lists redirecting or erroring URLs
rules.description: Sitemap URLs return redirects or 4xx/5xx. Sitemaps should list final, canonical, 200 URLs.
rules.fix: Replace each sitemap URL with its final 200 destination, or remove it.
rules.verify: Fetch all sitemap URLs; confirm 200 without redirects.

rules.title: Sitemap lists non-canonical URLs
rules.description: Sitemap URLs declare a rel=canonical pointing to another URL. Sitemaps should only list canonical URLs.
rules.fix: List the canonical target in the sitemap instead.
rules.verify: Re-crawl and compare sitemap URLs with declared canonicals.

rules.title: Possible soft 404
rules.description: The page returns 200 but its title/heading looks like an error page ("not found", "404"). Google reports such pages as soft 404 and does not index them.
rules.fix: Return a real 404/410 status for missing content, or add real content.
rules.verify: Fetch the URL and check status vs. content.

sources.title: Google: HTTP status codes, network and DNS errors

rules.title: Content depends on client-side JavaScript
rules.description: The raw HTML has almost no text but has a JS mount point and scripts. Google renders JavaScript, but rendering is deferred and other crawlers (including many AI crawlers) may not execute JS at all.
rules.fix: Use server-side rendering, static generation or pre-rendering for primary content and links.
rules.verify: Compare raw HTML vs. rendered DOM (searvex crawl --render).

rules.title: Rendered page differs from raw HTML on key signals
rules.description: Title, canonical, meta robots or links differ between the raw HTML and the JavaScript-rendered DOM. Google may skip rendering when raw HTML has noindex, and conflicting signals are unreliable.
rules.fix: Emit the final title, canonical and robots directives in the server HTML; do not change them with JavaScript.
rules.verify: Re-run with --render and confirm raw and rendered values match.
rules.appliesWhen: Only when JS rendering is enabled (--render).

rules.title: HTML document exceeds 15 MB
rules.description: Google crawlers fetch the first 15 MB of a file; content beyond that is not considered for indexing.
rules.fix: Reduce inline data (JSON state, base64 images) and paginate very long pages.
